acceptance_criteria: SPEC.md pins a concrete reproducible MoE baseline/model/data configuration or a clearly identified minimal proxy plus an explicit later-scale validation boundary.
SPEC.md defines numeric domains for all five control coordinates and a bounded Sobol/space-filling E1 design with a declared seed policy.
The measurement contract covers router entropy, expert load/use, imbalance, capacity/drop/overflow, loss, gradients/updates, and timing/state variables required by the mode estimator.
The mode-estimation protocol is frozen before execution and produces dominant complex eigenvalue/frequency/damping or growth estimates with window/uncertainty sensitivity checks.
Explicit predeclared rules distinguish ordinary collapse, damped oscillation, persistent oscillation, and divergent instability.

Null tests cover optimizer-memory ringing, capacity clipping/drop periodicity, data/batch periodicity, measurement-window sensitivity, stochastic router switching, and non-normal transient amplification.
The E1 artifact contract is sufficient to reproduce every sampled point, seed, observable trace, fitted local model, classification, and candidate-surface score.

A candidate surface may be nominated only under recurring controlled complex-mode behavior, coherent parameter dependence, cross-seed recurrence, observable regimes on both sides, and evidence against declared simpler nulls.
SPEC.md states an explicit resource-escalation trigger for any larger-GPU or materially larger run; no such escalation is implied by Charter admission.
The return path allows ACCELERATE, ACTIVE, NARROW, HOLD, or RETIRE, and treats a negative result as a successful discriminating outcome.
constraints: The work package must not assume that a Hopf/flutter boundary exists.

Ordinary expert collapse, router noise, optimizer ringing, capacity clipping, data/batch periodicity, measurement-window artifacts, and non-normal transient amplification are mandatory null explanations.
The theoretical label Hopf remains provisional unless its mathematical conditions are separately established.
No material compute, A100/H100-scale campaign, external service, external publication, partnership, or product commitment is authorized by this Charter projection.
E1 must use the smallest compute envelope capable of discriminating the declared null models; a larger envelope requires bounded resource justification and applicable authorization.
Analysis windows, mode-selection rules, classification thresholds, and candidate-surface nomination rules must be frozen before continuation results are examined.
Negative and null results must be retained as first-class evidence.
Repository artifacts are a local authoring projection; production work-package authority remains subject to the INTELLECT Constitution and AETHER-backed history.
payload.purpose: Determine whether sparse mixture-of-experts training systems possess a reproducible Hopf/flutter-like oscillatory instability boundary that is mechanistically distinguishable from ordinary expert collapse, stochastic router switching, optimizer-memory ringing, capacity clipping/drop periodicity, data/batch periodicity, measurement-window artifacts, or non-normal transient amplification.
payload.scope: Pre-register and, only after applicable Charter/review gates clear, execute a bounded five-dimensional E1 reconnaissance over router learning rate, routing temperature, load-balancing gain, capacity factor, and optimizer-memory strength. The first work-package deliverable is the frozen experimental design: baseline/model/data identity, Sobol design, seed policy, observable vector, complex-mode estimator, classification rules, null tests, artifact contract, and resource-escalation trigger. Any later E2 surface nomination or E3 continuation must be based on predeclared selection rules and preserved negative evidence.
